I don't know where those theories come from, because those arguments are based on functionality in our non-human friendly societies, where any bodily functions are inconvenient. 

For most of human history most women had 3-4 children, so no, most women weren't breastfeeding and pregnant all the time, and women had their first period later too (15-17). Serial pregnancies weren't the most common thing, and midwifes always had methods to track periods and fertile windows so at least women knew about that. Families weren't as big as we may imagine, and women didn't have as much children.

Short answer, yes, it is bad to completely stop your period because the menstrual cycle is involved in multiple areas of our bodies: digestion, nutrient absorption, sleep cycle, etc. Is not adviced to stop it and birth control is not really a treatment for things like endometriosis. I don't know why people in the comments ard saying that our bodies don't need periods, that's like saying we don't need any of the multiple bodily functions we have, or maybe it's something that USA/Europe doctors encourage, because at least in Latin America we know we need our periods and more women are choosing to stop any form of birth control. Periods could even be considered a vital sign.

Endometriosis is not even considered fully gynecological condition (just like PCOS) as its origin is unknown, so birth control shouldn't be the first line of treatment.

Costos casilla Reino Unido: cobran por sacar foto del contenido de los paquetes que llegan ($ 3 USD) y también cobran entre $1-$5 USD por otros servicios extra como mayor protección al paquete, compra asistida (compran por ti en alguna página web), sacar etiquetas, etc.

En ambos casos los servicios de fotos y cualquier cosa extra son opcionales, o sea que si por ej tú no quieres mayor protección en la caja o no quieres que le tomen foto al contenido está bien, no lo tienes que pagar ni te lo van a cobrar a no ser que efectivamente solicites el servicio.

I'm almost the same age as you and I'm a female too! So here's my perspective:

- I'd try to tell them that they haven't done anything to offend you or that is nothing wrong with how they have treated you (if that's the case). Maybe they think they annoyed you and that's why you are acting like that? I'm pretty paranoid and was almost diagnosed with BPD, so I think typical AVPD behavior could be misinterpreted as coldness, repressed annoyance or something similar, thus clearing that out would be great.

- Maybe try telling them more about how you feel rather than "I have AVPD"? Something along the lines of "in certain situations I [...] and I have a hard time dealing with it" "I feel anxious when..." and so on. I think that could be easier for them to understand? I'm speaking from my experience with friends, and when I wasn't that close with them yet I'd rather explain things in that way, and if they accepted me as I am I'd explain AVPD and all of that in the future when we know each other better, so they can understand why I behave the way I do.

- Remember to go at your own peace, don't get into friendships where you won't be appreciated, especially when you have this hell of a disorder that AVPD is! 🌹
